title: Distribution Functions and Moments of Harmonically Trapped Inertial Run-and-Tumble Particles in a Shear-Thickening Medium
abstract: We study the dynamics of an athermal inertial active particle confined in a harmonic potential and moving through shear-thickening media in one dimension. The activity is modeled using a symmetric dichotomous noise of strength $Σ$ and flipping rate $λ$, which mimics a run-and-tumble particle. The shear-thickening response of the medium is incorporated through a velocity-dependent viscous force of the form $g(v) \sim \tan(v)$. Starting from the Fokker-Planck equations corresponding to the particle's dynamics, we numerically compute the time-dependent joint probability density function $f(x,v,t)$ using a finite-volume upwind scheme. Next, we numerically solve the particle's equations of motion to obtain the steady-state position $P_s(x)$ and velocity $W_s(v)$ distributions and compare them with the marginal distributions obtained from $f(x,v,t)$ at sufficiently large $t$. The two approaches show excellent agreement. Both $P_s(x)$ and $W_s(v)$ exhibit several intriguing transitions as $λ$ is varied, and they eventually approach Gaussian-like profiles at sufficiently large $λ$. Our study of the time-dependent position-velocity correlation, $\langle xv \rangle(t)$, shows that larger values of $λ$ lead to faster relaxation to the steady state when all other parameters are held constant.
summary: This work analyzes the statistical mechanics of an inertial active particle moving in a shear-thickening medium under harmonic confinement. By solving the associated Fokker-Planck equations and comparing results with direct simulations, the authors characterize how the particle's steady-state distributions change with the noise flipping rate. The findings reveal a transition from localized behavior at low noise to Gaussian fluctuations at high noise, providing insights into active matter transport in complex fluids.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics and steady-state statistical properties of an inertial run-and-tumble particle confined in a harmonic potential while moving through a shear-thickening medium.
main_result: The steady-state position and velocity distributions exhibit intriguing transitions as the noise flipping rate ($\lambda$) is varied, approaching Gaussian profiles for large $\lambda$. Furthermore, the relaxation time to steady state is found to decrease as $\lambda$ increases.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using the Fokker-Planck equation approach, solved numerically via a finite-volume upwind scheme, and validated by comparing results with particle-based simulations of the equations of motion.
model_or_system: The system models an athermal inertial active particle subject to harmonic confinement and a velocity-dependent viscous drag force characteristic of a shear-thickening medium. Activity is introduced via symmetric dichotomous noise mimicking run-and-tumble motion.
key_observables: Time-dependent joint probability density function $f(x,v,t)$, steady-state position $P_s(x)$ and velocity $W_s(v)$ distributions, and the time-dependent position-velocity correlation $\langle xv angle(t)$.
important_parameters: Flipping rate ($\lambda$), noise strength ($\Sigma$), and harmonic confinement constant ($k$). Key regimes include low $\lambda$ (near fixed points) and high $\lambda$ (fluctuating around $x=0$).
main_assumptions: The active force is modeled as symmetric dichotomous noise, and the analysis is restricted to one dimension ($d=1$). The numerical methods rely on finite-volume upwind schemes for the FP equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the joint PDF $f_s(x, v)$ across different $\lambda$ values, showing concentration near fixed points at low $\lambda$ and spreading towards Gaussian forms at high $\lambda$. They also show the time evolution of moments like $\langle x^2 angle$ and $\langle xv angle(t)$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing equations (EOMs and FP equations) for the particle dynamics. It then details the numerical methods (finite-volume upwind scheme) used to solve the FP equations. Finally, it presents and analyzes the results concerning the steady-state distributions and time correlations as a function of the noise parameters.
why_interesting: The combination of active matter physics (run-and-tumble) with non-Newtonian fluid dynamics (shear-thickening) provides a rich platform for studying non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. The transition from deterministic fixed-point behavior to diffusive Gaussian behavior as noise increases is a key physical insight.
